squareQuips.HD-SQUARE-TS01: “I once sat on a wall to admire the view. Lovely view. I do not recommend the wall.”
squareQuips.HD-SQUARE-TS02: “Romance in this kingdom has a deadline. Paperwork does not. I have been waiting on a wall permit for six years.”
squareQuips.HD-SQUARE-TS03: “Every princess keeps a schedule. Learn it. Nothing says ‘devoted’ like waiting at an empty quay, chatting to a gull.”
squareQuips.HD-SQUARE-TS04: “All the king’s horses came to help me once. Lovely animals. Hopeless with glue.”
squareQuips.HD-SQUARE-TS05: “If the court asks whether you know what you are doing, test that theory first. I said yes once. Then I was on a wall.”
squareQuips.HD-SQUARE-TS06: “People call me difficult to put back together. The glue merchants call me a valued long-term customer.”
squareQuips.HD-SQUARE-TS07: “A locked milestone is not an angry princess. The milestone is a number. The princess will tell you exactly what you did.”
squareQuips.HD-SQUARE-TS08: “In an important conversation, the cleverest thing you can say is often a question. I have many questions. Most of them are about walls.”
squareQuips.HD-SQUARE-TS09: “My advice is free. The premium package is the same advice, delivered from a lower wall.”
squareQuips.HD-SQUARE-TS10: “The palace believes every problem needs a committee. I believe every problem needs a chair. Low to the ground. With arms.”
squareQuips.HD-SQUARE-TS11: “When a mermaid tells you the water is where she belongs, believe the expert. I feel the same way about the ground.”
squareQuips.HD-SQUARE-TS12: “A dragon princess can open her own doors, and most walls. You may still ask whether she would like company.”

activities.ACT-CHA-READ-L01: You read a chapter called “Openers for Royalty.” Opener four is just winking. You close the book before it can suggest opener five.
activities.ACT-CHA-READ-L02: You practice a line on the mirror. The mirror loves it. The mirror is not a princess.
activities.ACT-CHA-TALK-L01: You chat with the townsfolk. One question to a baker earns you twenty minutes on sourdough and a free roll.
activities.ACT-CHA-TALK-L02: Nobody grades you. Several people ask your name. Progress.
activities.ACT-INT-BOOK-L01: You read two histories of the same obscure custom. They disagree about everything, including the custom.
activities.ACT-INT-BOOK-L02: You leave with one answer and three better questions. The librarian calls this a good day.
activities.ACT-INT-ORACLE-L01: The oracle answers instantly, with great confidence and three footnotes. Two of the footnotes cite the oracle. You check the sources.
activities.ACT-INT-ORACLE-L02: Asked to show its work, the oracle concedes that “probably” was doing most of it.
activities.ACT-STR-CAL-L01: You work through a careful set of push-ups and squats. Form over noise. Mostly.
activities.ACT-STR-CAL-L02: The floor survives another session. So, narrowly, do you.
activities.ACT-STR-GUILD-L01: You run drills on the guild’s ordinary equipment. A veteran watches, says “Hm,” and leaves. You decide that was praise.
activities.ACT-STR-GUILD-L02: The training dummy remains intact. The guild counts this as a win for everyone, including the dummy.
activities.ACT-KIN-DOG-L01: You refill the water bowls and find the garden dogs some shade. One of them sits on your foot so you can’t leave.
activities.ACT-KIN-DOG-L02: The reviews are in: one wagging tail, one sneeze, no numbers.
activities.ACT-KIN-LITTER-L01: You pick up litter around the square. The flowerbeds look better. A pigeon looks betrayed.
activities.ACT-KIN-LITTER-L02: Nobody throws you a parade. Given what parades leave behind, that’s for the best.
